title: Pollo alla Romana
subtitle: Roman braised chicken with peppers and tomatoes
excerpt: Pollo alla romana is a classic Roman summer braise: chicken pieces slowly cooked with red and yellow peppers, tomatoes, garlic, white wine, and fresh marjoram. The peppers melt into the sauce. It is one of the most characteristic dishes of Roman home cooking in summer, when peppers are at their best.
sourceNotes: Pollo alla romana is a classic of Roman trattoria cooking and home cooking. The combination of chicken, peppers, tomatoes, and white wine is found in Ada Boni's La Cucina Romana (1929) and has remained a standard of Roman cooking since. The dish is closely related to pollo alla cacciatora (hunter's chicken) but uses peppers as the defining ingredient.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves if made a day ahead and reheated gently.

content.text: The chicken is browned first in olive oil, then the peppers, tomatoes, and wine go in and everything braises together. The peppers must cook long enough to completely soften -- they should melt into the sauce, not remain firm. Use a mix of red and yellow peppers for colour and sweetness.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium-high heat. Season {{chicken-thigh}} chicken thighs with {{salt-table}} salt. Brown well on both sides, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add {{garlic}} garlic to the pan and cook for 1 minute. Add {{pepper-red}} red and {{pepper-yellow}} yellow pepper strips. Cook for 5 minutes until starting to soften.

Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes, {{marjoram}} marjoram, and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Return the chicken to the pan. Cover and simmer over very low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers have melted into the sauce. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve with crusty bread or polenta.

items.symptom: The peppers are still firm after 40 minutes
items.cause: The heat was too high, causing the sauce to reduce before the peppers softened.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and continue cooking covered over very low heat. Peppers need sustained, gentle heat to soften completely. They should melt into ribbons in the sauce.

content.text: Pollo alla romana is the summer version of the Roman braised chicken tradition. Peppers (peperoni) become central to Roman cooking in July and August, when the Roman campagna produces large, sweet, thick-walled varieties. The dish appears in Ada Boni's La Cucina Romana, the defining cookbook of Roman cuisine, published in 1929 and still in print. Marjoram (not oregano) is the herb of Roman chicken cooking.
